when.night: Phrase inserted into a story sentence, e.g. 'your best game came after midnight'. Time of day for matches played late at night. Keep short, about 14 characters.
when.morning: Phrase inserted into a story sentence, e.g. 'you played most in the morning'. Time of day. Keep short, about 14 characters.
when.afternoon: Phrase inserted into a story sentence, e.g. 'you played most in the afternoon'. Time of day. Keep short, about 16 characters.
when.evening: Phrase inserted into a story sentence, e.g. 'you played most in the evening'. Time of day. Keep short, about 14 characters.

frame.deck_versus: Joins a story's sub-headline ({deck}) with a comparison sentence ({versus}), e.g. {deck} = 'Eight wins in ten.', {versus} = 'Up from six last week.' Adapt spacing if needed. Keep short.

masthead.name: Newspaper title at the top of every Dispatch paper. Dispatch is the feature name, keep it as a newspaper name. 'Deadlock+' stays untranslated. Keep short, about 18 characters.
masthead.edition_weekly: Masthead line on a Weekly edition paper. Keep short, about 14 characters.
masthead.edition_monthly: Masthead line on a Monthly edition paper. Keep short, about 15 characters.
masthead.edition_live: Masthead line on the live paper that updates during the current week. Keep short, about 16 characters.
masthead.issue: Masthead issue line on a printed paper. {volume} = volume number, e.g. 2. {number} = issue number, e.g. 14. Newspaper style. Keep short, about 28 characters.
masthead.issue_live: Masthead issue line on the live 'This week so far' paper. {volume} = volume number, e.g. 2. Keep short, about 13 characters.
masthead.edition_collectors: Masthead line on a Collector's Copy, the paper printed at the end of a ranked season. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. Keep short, about 27 characters.
masthead.edition_year_end: Masthead line on the Year-End Special, the yearly paper with a fold-out poster. Keep short, about 16 characters.

dispatch.paper_label: Screen reader label for a paper. {name} = newspaper title, e.g. Deadlock+ Dispatch. {edition} = edition, e.g. Weekly Edition. {date} = date, e.g. Oct 12.
dispatch.player_fallback: Name shown on a paper when the player has no Steam name. Keep short, about 14 characters.
dispatch.photo_caption: Caption under the hero photo on a paper. {hero} = Deadlock hero name, e.g. Haze (game term, match the game). {count} = number of games with that hero in this edition, e.g. 7. Covers singular and plural.

stamp.so_far: Small stamp on the live paper meaning the week is not finished. Keep short, about 6 characters.
stamp.collectors: Small stamp on a Collector's Copy paper (end of ranked season edition). Keep short, about 16 characters.

section.stories: Section title on a paper for the extra stories. Newspaper style. Keep short, about 11 characters.
section.numbers: Section title on a paper above the stats box (matches, record, win rate). Keep short, about 14 characters.
section.best_game_weekly: Section title on a Weekly edition above the best match of the week. Keep short, about 16 characters.
section.best_game_monthly: Section title on a Monthly edition above the best match of the month. Keep short, about 17 characters.
section.heroes: Section title on a paper above the list of heroes played. Heroes are Deadlock game terms. Keep short, about 11 characters.
section.people: Section title on a paper above the box about teammates and the player who beat you most. Playful, like 'the company you keep'. Keep short, about 20 characters.
section.best_game_collectors: Section title on a Collector's Copy above the best match of the season. Keep short, about 18 characters.
section.best_game_year_end: Section title on the Year-End Special above the best match of the year. Keep short, about 16 characters.

numbers.matches: Label in the stats box on a paper, above the number of matches played. Keep short, about 7 characters.
numbers.record: Label in the stats box on a paper, above the win and loss record. Keep short, about 6 characters.
numbers.record_value: Win and loss record in the stats box. {wins} = wins, e.g. 12. {losses} = losses, e.g. 8. Example result: 12-8. Keep the numbers and a short separator.
numbers.winrate: Label in the stats box on a paper, above the win percentage. Keep short, about 8 characters.
numbers.playtime: Label in the stats box on a paper, above total time played. Keep short, about 11 characters.
numbers.kda: Label in the stats box on a paper, above average kills, deaths and assists per game. Keep K/D/A as the game shows it. Keep short, about 12 characters.
numbers.playtime_value: Time played in the stats box. {hours} = hours, e.g. 14.5. 'h' is the hours abbreviation. Keep short, about 9 characters.

heroes.games: Column header in the hero report on a paper, number of games per hero. Keep short, about 5 characters.
heroes.wins: Column header in the hero report on a paper, number of wins per hero. Keep short, about 3 characters.
heroes.time: Column header in the hero report on a paper, time played per hero. Keep short, about 4 characters.

best_game.net_worth: Stat line under the best match on a paper. {value} = net worth number, e.g. 41.2k. Net worth is a Deadlock game term, match the game's translation.

people.mate_line: Line in the teammates box on a paper. {count} = matches played with that teammate, e.g. 6. {wins} = how many of those were won, e.g. 4. Covers singular and plural.
people.nemesis: Heading in the people box on a paper for the player who beat you most. Wanted poster style. Keep short, about 11 characters.
people.nemesis_line: Line under the nemesis in the people box. {matches} = number of matches against them, e.g. 5. {count} = times they beat you, e.g. 3. Covers singular ('Beat you once in 5') and plural.

export.lead_story: Option in the Dispatch export panel: export only the lead story as an image. Keep short, about 10 characters.

aspect.tall: Image shape option in the export panel (tall, portrait). Keep short, about 4 characters.
aspect.square: Image shape option in the export panel (square). Keep short, about 6 characters.
aspect.wide: Image shape option in the export panel (wide, landscape). Keep short, about 4 characters.

export.saved: Toast. A Dispatch image was saved to a file.
export.copied: Toast. A Dispatch image was copied to the clipboard.
export.render_failed: Error toast. Making the Dispatch image failed. Asks the user to try again.
export.spread: Joins two page names for a two-page spread export. {left} and {right} = page names, e.g. 'Front page' and 'Heroes'. Keep short.

page.title: Page title of the Dispatch page, a newspaper about the player's matches. Feature name, keep it consistent as a newspaper name. Keep short, about 8 characters.

page.replay: Button on the Dispatch page that replays the paper's reveal animation. Keep short, about 17 characters.
page.table: Button on the Dispatch page that switches to the table view, where papers lie like on a desk. Keep short, about 5 characters.

shelf.print_not_enough: Message in the shelf: there are too few matches to print this edition.

year_end.player_of_the_year: Title on the Year-End Special cover naming the player of the year. Keep short, about 18 characters.
year_end.title: Headline on the Year-End Special. {year} = year, e.g. 2026. {player} = player name, e.g. Sammi. Keep short, about 28 characters.
year_end.title_anonymous: Headline on the Year-End Special when the player has no name. {year} = year, e.g. 2026. Keep short, about 26 characters.

cover.matches: Cover stat label on the Year-End Special, under the number of matches. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 7 characters.
cover.hours: Cover stat label on the Year-End Special, under the number of hours. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 5 characters.
cover.days: Cover stat label on the Year-End Special, under the number of days played. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 11 characters.
cover.star: Cover line on the Year-End Special for the star hero. {hero} = Deadlock hero name, e.g. Haze (game term). {count} = games with that hero, e.g. 120. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 22 characters.

year_end.streak: Label on the Year-End Special for the longest winning streak. Keep short, about 11 characters.
year_end.streak_line: Text after a streak number on the Year-End Special, e.g. '9 wins in a row'. Singular and plural. Keep short.
year_end.flap: Text on the flap of the Year-End Special cover: a fold-out poster is inside. Keep short, about 22 characters.
year_end.unfold: Button on the Year-End Special that unfolds the poster. Keep short, about 27 characters.
year_end.fold_up: Button that folds the Year-End poster back up. Keep short, about 7 characters.
year_end.band_issue: Band line on the Year-End poster. {edition} = edition name, e.g. Year-End Special. {issue} = issue text, e.g. Vol. 1 · No. 1. Keep short, about 19 characters.

numbers.title: Heading of the stats section on the Year-End poster. Keep short, about 19 characters.
numbers.hours: Stat label on the Year-End poster, hours played. Keep short, about 5 characters.
numbers.days: Stat label on the Year-End poster, number of days played. Keep short, about 11 characters.
numbers.heroes: Stat label on the Year-End poster, number of different heroes played. Heroes are a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 12 characters.
numbers.longest_match: Stat label on the Year-End poster, longest single match. Keep short, about 13 characters.
numbers.longest_session: Stat label on the Year-End poster, longest play session in one sitting. Keep short, about 15 characters.
numbers.session_value: Stat value on the Year-End poster for the longest session. {count} = games in that session, e.g. 9. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 13 characters.

year_end.top_heroes: Heading on the Year-End poster for the most played heroes. Singular when one hero. {count} = number of heroes, e.g. 3. Heroes are a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 18 characters.
year_end.hero_of_the_year: Heading on the Year-End poster for the most played hero. Hero is a Deadlock game term. Keep short, about 16 characters.
year_end.hero_games: Hero stat on the Year-End poster. {count} = games with the hero, e.g. 120. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 13 characters.
year_end.hero_wins: Hero stat on the Year-End poster. {count} = wins with the hero, e.g. 70. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 12 characters.
year_end.hero_hours: Hero stat on the Year-End poster. {count} = hours with the hero, e.g. 85. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 13 characters.
year_end.grade: Grade badge on the Year-End poster. {grade} = a letter grade, e.g. A+ or B. Keep short, about 13 characters.
year_end.ran_with: Label on the Year-End poster above the teammate the player played with most. Keep short, about 8 characters.
year_end.nemesis: Label on the Year-End poster above the player who beat you most. Keep short, about 7 characters.

month.title: Heading of the monthly activity chart on the Year-End poster. Keep short, about 14 characters.
month.sub: Caption under the monthly chart title on the Year-End poster. Keep short, about 14 characters.
month.busiest: Label on the monthly chart marking the busiest month. {count} = matches in that month, e.g. 85. Keep short, about 17 characters.

inside.kicker: Small line above the title on the inside of the Year-End poster. Dispatch is the newspaper name, keep it. 'Deadlock+' stays untranslated. Keep short, about 27 characters.
inside.title: Title on the inside of the Year-End poster. Keep short, about 18 characters.

year_end.unfolded: Screen reader announcement: the Year-End poster is now unfolded.
year_end.folded: Screen reader announcement: the Year-End poster is now folded up.

collectors.title: Masthead title of the Collector's Copy, shown at the top of its pages. Same word as the newspaper name. Keep short, about 8 characters.
collectors.arc: Line on the Collector's Copy cover. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. Keep short, about 24 characters.
collectors.cover_label: Screen reader label for the Collector's Copy cover. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. {rank} = peak rank name, e.g. Ritualist 3. Match the game's rank names.
collectors.peak_reached: Caption on the Collector's Copy. {date} = a date, e.g. Mar 14. Says when the season peak rank was reached.
collectors.peak_label: Label for the best rank reached in the season, on the Collector's Copy. Keep short, about 11 characters.
collectors.unranked: Shown in the Collector's Copy when there is no rank to show for the season. Match the game's wording if it has one. Keep short, about 8 characters.
collectors.the_climb: Label on the Collector's Copy cover for the rank progress story. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.ranked_record: Label on the Collector's Copy cover above the season's ranked win and loss record. Keep short, about 13 characters.
collectors.record_value: Win and loss record, e.g. 24-18. {wins} = number of wins, {losses} = number of losses. Keep the order wins first.
collectors.teaser: Teaser line on the Collector's Copy cover, promising the pages inside. Keep short, about 40 characters.
collectors.your_copy: Small label on the Collector's Copy cover marking it as the player's own copy. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.copy_no: Abbreviation for 'number' before the copy's serial number, e.g. No. 128. Keep short, about 3 characters.
collectors.sealed: Stamp on the sealed Collector's Copy sleeve, like a mark of authenticity. Keep short, about 18 characters.
collectors.sticker_top: Top line of a sticker on the sealed Collector's Copy sleeve. Reads with the next two stickers as 'Collector's Copy, Do not open'. Keep short, about 11 characters.
collectors.sticker_main: Big middle word of the sleeve sticker, after 'Collector's'. Keep short, about 4 characters.
collectors.sticker_note: Small bottom line of the sleeve sticker, a playful warning. Keep short, about 11 characters.
collectors.tear: Short label on the tear strip of the Collector's Copy sleeve. Also the action word for opening it. Keep short, about 4 characters.
collectors.tear_label: Screen reader label for the button that opens the sealed Collector's Copy sleeve.
collectors.tear_open: Button text that opens the sealed Collector's Copy. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.back_to_cover: Button that goes back to the Collector's Copy cover. Keep short, about 17 characters.
collectors.reseal: Button that closes the Collector's Copy again, putting the sleeve back on. Keep short, about 6 characters.
collectors.previous_page: Button and aria label to go to the previous page of the Collector's Copy.
collectors.next_page: Button and aria label to go to the next page of the Collector's Copy.
collectors.inside_label: Screen reader label for the inner pages of the Collector's Copy. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3.
collectors.climb_title: Headline of the Collector's Copy page showing the season's rank progress. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.climb_deck: Subtitle under the 'The Climb' headline in the Collector's Copy. Explains the chart: one step per ranked match, a star marks the best rank. About 86 characters.
collectors.chart_label: Aria label for the rank over time chart on the Collector's Copy climb page.
collectors.callout_peak: Callout on the climb chart pointing at the best rank of the season. Keep short, about 4 characters.
collectors.promotions: Label on the climb page for how many times the player moved up a rank. Keep short, about 10 characters.
collectors.demotions: Label on the climb page for how many times the player dropped a rank. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.ranked_matches: Label on the climb page for the number of ranked matches played in the season. Keep short, about 14 characters.
collectors.started: Label for the rank the player had at the start of the season, on the climb page. Keep short, about 7 characters.
collectors.finished: Label for the rank the player had at the end of the season, on the climb page. Keep short, about 8 characters.
collectors.climb_up: Net rank gain over the season, on the climb page. {count} = subranks gained, e.g. 5. A subrank is one step inside a rank, e.g. Ritualist 2 to 3. About 17 characters.
collectors.climb_down: Net rank loss over the season, on the climb page. {count} = subranks lost, e.g. 3. A subrank is one step inside a rank. Keep the minus sign. About 17 characters.
collectors.climb_held: Shown on the climb page when the player ended the season at the same rank they started. Keep short, about 13 characters.
collectors.folio: Page footer of the Collector's Copy inner pages. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. {page} = page label, e.g. Page 2. Keep short, about 36 characters.
collectors.reached: Caption for when a rank was reached. {date} = a date, e.g. Mar 14. Keep short, about 14 characters.
collectors.match_of: Caption naming one ranked match in the season. {n} = its position, e.g. 12. {total} = all ranked matches, e.g. 48.
collectors.record: Label for the win and loss record, on the Collector's Copy peak page. Keep short, about 6 characters.
collectors.won: Label for wins, on the Collector's Copy peak page. Keep short, about 3 characters.
collectors.best_streak: Label for the longest win streak of the season, on the Collector's Copy peak page. Keep short, about 15 characters.
collectors.carried: Label for the hero that carried the player's climb, on the Collector's Copy peak page. Keep short, about 17 characters.
collectors.hero_games: Number of games played on a hero, in the Collector's Copy. {count} = number, e.g. 14. Keep short, about 13 characters.
collectors.hero_wins: Number of wins on a hero, in the Collector's Copy. {count} = number, e.g. 9. Keep short, about 12 characters.
collectors.cert_title: Title of the certificate of authenticity at the end of the Collector's Copy. Keep short, about 27 characters.
collectors.cert_body: Text of the certificate in the Collector's Copy. {name} = player name. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. {count} = number of ranked matches, e.g. 48.
collectors.cert_body_anon: Certificate text in the Collector's Copy when the player name is hidden. {season} = season name, e.g. Season 3. {count} = number of ranked matches, e.g. 48.
collectors.issued_by: Label on the certificate before the issuer, e.g. Issued by Deadlock+. Keep short, about 9 characters.
collectors.copy_number: Label on the certificate before the copy's serial number. Keep short, about 8 characters.
collectors.page: Page label. {page} = page number, e.g. 3. Used in the Dispatch reader and export. Keep short, about 11 characters.

fact.kda: Fact label on the numbers page: average kills, deaths and assists per match. Keep K/D/A. Keep short, about 13 characters.
fact.kda_note: Small note under the K/D/A fact. {kills} = total kills in the month, e.g. 312. About 24 characters.
fact.longest_match: Fact label on the numbers page: the longest match of the month. Keep short, about 13 characters.
fact.longest_match_value: Duration of the longest match. {minutes} = minutes, e.g. 54. Keep short, about 13 characters.
fact.longest_match_note: Small note under the longest match: it counts the full match, start to finish. Keep short, about 15 characters.
fact.longest_session: Fact label on the numbers page: the longest run of matches played in one sitting. Keep short, about 15 characters.
fact.longest_session_value: Number of games in the longest session. {matches} = number, e.g. 9. Keep short, about 15 characters.
fact.longest_session_note: Small note under the longest session. {duration} = length of time, e.g. 4h 20m. {date} = a date, e.g. Oct 12. About 18 characters.
fact.busiest_day: Fact label on the numbers page: the day with the most matches. Keep short, about 11 characters.
fact.busiest_day_note: Small note under the busiest day fact. {matches} = number of matches that day, e.g. 12. About 17 characters.
fact.days_played: Fact label on the numbers page: how many days the player played. Keep short, about 11 characters.
fact.days_played_note: Small note under days played. {days} = days in the month, e.g. 31. About 22 characters.
fact.night: Fact label on the numbers page: the share of matches played after midnight. Keep short, about 14 characters.
fact.night_note: Small note under the after midnight fact, following a percentage. Keep the 00:00-06:00 time range. Keep short, about 23 characters.

calendar.title: Heading above the calendar of the month on the Monthly edition. {month} = month name, e.g. October. Keep short, about 20 characters.
calendar.legend_won: Calendar legend entry for days with more wins than losses. Keep short, about 9 characters.
calendar.legend_lost: Calendar legend entry for days with more losses than wins, or an equal number. Keep short, about 19 characters.
calendar.day: Screen reader label for one calendar day. {date} = a date, e.g. Oct 12. {count} = matches that day. {wins} = how many were won.
calendar.day_empty: Screen reader label for a calendar day without matches. {date} = a date, e.g. Oct 12.

heroes.fallback_deck: Subtitle on the heroes page when there is no custom text. {count} = games on the hero. {wins} = games won. {month} = month name, e.g. October. About 60 characters.
heroes.share_label: Label next to a percentage on the heroes page. {hero} = hero name, e.g. Haze. Match the game's hero names. About 25 characters.
heroes.rotation: Heading for the list of heroes played in the month, like a sports team rotation. Keep short, about 12 characters.
heroes.tried: Count of different heroes played. {count} = number, e.g. 7. {month} = month name, e.g. October. About 31 characters.
heroes.col_games: Table column header on the heroes page: number of games. Keep short, about 5 characters.
heroes.col_record: Table column header on the heroes page: win and loss record. Keep short, about 3 characters.
heroes.col_played: Table column header on the heroes page: share of games played on that hero. Keep short, about 6 characters.
heroes.record: Win and loss record in the heroes table, e.g. 9-4. {wins} = wins, {losses} = losses. Wins first.

best.fallback_headline: Headline of the best game page when there is no custom headline. {hero} = hero name, e.g. Haze. Match the game's hero names. {kda} = kills/deaths/assists, e.g. 14/2/9. About 13 characters.
best.kills: Stat label on the best game page. Match the game's wording. Keep short, about 5 characters.
best.deaths: Stat label on the best game page. Match the game's wording. Keep short, about 6 characters.
best.assists: Stat label on the best game page. Match the game's wording. Keep short, about 7 characters.
best.net_worth: Stat label on the best game page for souls collected. Match the game's wording for net worth. Keep short, about 9 characters.
best.grade: Stat label on the best game page for the performance grade (a letter like A or S). Keep short, about 5 characters.
best.also: Heading above other strong games of the month, below the best game. Keep short, about 15 characters.

people.title: Headline of the people page in the Monthly edition, about the players the user met most. Keep short, about 20 characters.
people.most_wanted: Label on the people page for the opponent who beat the player most, like a wanted poster. Keep short, about 11 characters.

rank.start: Rank label on the Monthly edition for the rank at the start of the month. {month} = month name, e.g. October. Keep short, about 16 characters.
rank.end: Rank label on the Monthly edition for the rank at the end of the month. {month} = month name, e.g. October. Keep short, about 14 characters.
rank.peak: Rank label on the Monthly edition for the best rank reached in the month. Keep short, about 4 characters.

monthly.next_label: Label on the last Monthly page, above the date of the next issue. Keep short, about 10 characters.
monthly.next_line: Line on the last Monthly page. {month} = month name of the next issue, e.g. November. {date} = release date, e.g. Dec 1. About 19 characters.
monthly.close: Button that closes the opened Monthly edition book. Keep short, about 5 characters.
monthly.prev: Button and aria label to go to the previous pair of pages in the Monthly edition. Keep short, about 14 characters.
monthly.next: Button and aria label to go to the next pair of pages in the Monthly edition. Keep short, about 10 characters.

spread.cover: Aria label for the closed Monthly edition cover, shown as a page spread. Keep short, about 5 characters.
spread.pages: Aria label for a pair of facing pages. {from} and {to} = page numbers, e.g. 2 and 3.

mini.pair: Joins two short items on a mini paper, e.g. {first} = 12 matches, {second} = 8 wins. Keep the separator dot. Keep short, about 18 characters.
mini.the_monthly: Label on a mini paper in the table view for the Monthly edition. Keep short, about 11 characters.
mini.proof: Stamp on a mini paper for a trial print (a 'proof'). Keep short, about 5 characters.
mini.not_printed: Label on a mini paper that has not been printed yet. Keep short, about 15 characters.
mini.still_printing: Text on a mini paper that is still being printed. The line break is intentional, keep it. Keep short, about 14 characters.
mini.fold_out: Text on a mini Year-End paper about its fold-out poster. The line break is intentional, keep it. Keep short, about 15 characters.
mini.so_far_foot: Footer on the mini live paper. {count} = matches so far, e.g. 3. {day} = weekday the paper comes out, e.g. Sunday. Singular and plural. Keep short, about 27 characters.
mini.aria: Screen reader label for a mini paper. {kind} = edition type, e.g. Weekly. {date} = date, e.g. Oct 12. {detail} = extra info, e.g. 12 matches.

table.weeklies: Heading for the pile of Weekly editions on the Dispatch table. {label} = period, e.g. October 2026. Keep short, about 17 characters.
table.monthlies: Heading for the pile of Monthly editions on the Dispatch table. {label} = period, e.g. 2026. Keep short, about 18 characters.
table.close: Button on the Dispatch table that closes an opened pile or paper. Keep short, about 5 characters.
table.gather: Button on the Dispatch table that gathers the spread papers back into a pile. Keep short, about 17 characters.

dispatch.range_join: Word between two dates in a date range, e.g. 'Oct 5 to Oct 11'. Keep short.

share.kicker: Small heading above the title of the share sheet. Keep short, about 5 characters.
share.close: Close button in the share sheet. Keep short, about 5 characters.
share.format: Label in the share sheet above the choice of picture shape. Keep short, about 6 characters.
share.picture: Tab or option in the share sheet to share a still picture. Keep short, about 7 characters.
share.video: Tab or option in the share sheet to share a video. Keep short, about 5 characters.
share.pages: Label in the share sheet above the choice of which paper pages to include. Keep short, about 5 characters.
share.made_for: Label in the share sheet before the sites that fit the chosen shape. Keep short, about 8 characters.

where.tall: Share sheet list of sites for the tall format. Brand names stay untranslated. Keep short, about 21 characters.
where.square: Share sheet list of sites for the square format. Brand names stay untranslated. Keep short, about 18 characters.
where.wide: Share sheet list of sites for the wide format. Brand names stay untranslated. Keep short, about 10 characters.

share.chat_you: Sender name in the fake chat preview in the share sheet, meaning the user. Keep short, about 3 characters.
share.chat_today: Day divider in the fake chat preview in the share sheet. Keep short, about 5 characters.
share.preview_video: Screen reader label for the video preview in the share sheet. Keep short, about 13 characters.
share.retry: Button in the share sheet to retry after a failed video. Keep short, about 9 characters.
share.video_saved: Status in the share sheet: the video was saved. Keep short, about 11 characters.
share.video_meta: Video file details in the share sheet. {width} and {height} = pixels, e.g. 1080 and 1920. {seconds} = length, e.g. 12. MP4 stays. 's' = seconds abbreviation. Keep short, about 34 characters.
share.scenes: Label in the share sheet above the list of video scenes. Keep short, about 6 characters.
share.video_failed: Error text in the share sheet: the video could not be made.
